## Observed

- `transition_ticket(closed)` over MCP pins completion verification to `resolve_ref("HEAD", repo_root)` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:146`). The server's repo root is `REBAR_ROOT=/var/gerrit/site/mcp-code`.
- That workspace is refreshed (fetch plus fast-forward) only by `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` at container start.
- Autodeploy restarts the MCP container only when `MCP_PATHS` change (`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh:87`; `src/rebar`, the Dockerfile, the entrypoint, the compose file, `uv.lock`, `pyproject.toml`). A commit touching only docs, tests, `infra/terraform` or other paths advances main without refreshing the workspace.
- Reproduced 2026-11-11 21:50 PST (read-only SSM): main was b603c4544e8, a Terraform-only commit (infra/terraform/monitoring_bedrock_cost.tf); the live container rebar-mcp-aed975de61c7-8093 had MCP_CODE_DIR HEAD aed975de61c, one commit behind. A close over MCP in that window verifies against aed975de61c, and the close precheck cannot see b603c4544e8.

## Approach

Refresh the live workspace in place on the steady-state autodeploy tick, rather than changing which ref the close resolves (local CLI closes must keep verifying the caller's worktree HEAD).
- `infra/scripts/mcp-entrypoint.sh` gains a `--refresh-code` mode that runs the existing `refresh_code` (locked; refuses dirty or diverged trees; recovers an interrupted fast-forward).
- `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`: on the no-op tick, `mcp_refresh_code_workspace` reads the live backend's workspace HEAD and, when it is not `$TARGET`, runs `docker exec <live> sh /usr/local/bin/mcp-entrypoint.sh --refresh-code` (bounded at 300 s, like the mirror fetch). The freshness probe then checks that the workspace contains `$TARGET` (not merely the image commit), so a refresh that fails pages through the existing deploy_errors alarm.
- No config key, env var or flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A test reproduces the lag (workspace at an older commit, main advanced with no MCP image change) and shows the no-op tick fast-forwards it to the target without paging; a test shows a current workspace is not touched. Pinned in `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py`.
- [ ] `make verify` passes and the change lands through Gerrit.
- [ ] [non-codebase] After deploy, a non-MCP-path commit on main reaches the live workspace within a few autodeploy ticks without a container restart.
  provenance: environment=production rebar host i-00880b2c7f13527c5 (MCP container); principal=frontier operator role via SSM; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — read-only SSM read of MCP_CODE_DIR HEAD vs origin/main and the container name before and after a non-MCP commit lands
